author: shohei81
body:
## What
- move `--search` and `--ask-for-approval` to top-level `codex` flags instead of passing them to `codex exec`
- move other global CLI flags (`--profile`, `--sandbox`, `--full-auto`, `--add-dir`) to top-level as well so `exec resume` remains valid
- keep exec/resume-safe flags (`--json`, `--model`, `--config`, `--skip-git-repo-check`) on the `exec` subcommand
- harden JSONL parsing to capture structured tool calls from message content blocks (`tool_call` / `tool_use` / `function_call`), not only text-embedded `<tool_use>` tags
- add support for `response.*` event shapes as an additional parser path:
  - `response.output_item.added` / `response.output_item.done`
  - `response.output_text.delta` fallback aggregation
  - `response.completed` usage parsing + output fallback
  - `response.error` explicit failure handling
- accept SSE-style `data:`-prefixed JSONL lines (including `[DONE]` markers) for better compatibility with wrapped/forwarded streams
- improve process stream handling by draining stderr concurrently to avoid pipe pressure and to reliably surface stderr details on non-zero exits
- add safety adjustment for known API incompatibility: when `search=true` and resolved `reasoning_effort=minimal`, automatically use `low` and warn
- fix session persistence behavior so `get_or_create_session(session_id=...)` creates a session with that ID when missing (stable resume/cache linkage across restarts)
- add regression tests for command construction, structured tool-call parsing, response-event compatibility, SSE-line parsing, error propagation, stderr surfacing, and session-id persistence

## Why
Recent Codex CLI behavior rejects several flags when they are passed after `exec`/`exec resume` (for example `--search`, `--ask-for-approval`, `--sandbox`, `--profile`). That caused provider failures when those options were enabled.

Also, relying only on text-embedded tool-use tags is brittle. Structured item blocks and response-event shapes are now supported so provider behavior is stable across more JSON event variants.

Finally, the API currently rejects `web_search` when reasoning effort is `minimal`; without adjustment, those requests fail.

## Validation
- `uv run pytest -q`
- `uv run ruff check`
- manual smoke test with real CLI:
  - `codex --sandbox workspace-write exec ...`
  - `codex --sandbox workspace-write --ask-for-approval never exec resume ...`
  - `codex --search exec ... -c 'model_reasoning_effort="minimal"'` (reproduced incompatibility)

We only update position for a file after some time have passed and when tailer exist. But then we stopped position file before we stopped all tailers so if a file was ingested fast we never stored last read offset.

To fix this we need to stop position after all trailers have been stopped and we need to set lastUpdatedPosition to the start position.

author: joaquinbejar
body:
## Summary

Implement application-level error types that wrap domain and infrastructure errors with proper context preservation using thiserror.

## Changes

### InfrastructureError (new)
| Variant | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `Database` | Database connection/query errors |
| `Network` | Network connectivity errors |
| `MessageQueue` | Message broker errors |
| `Cache` | Cache system errors |
| `ExternalService` | Third-party service errors |
| `Configuration` | Config/setup errors |
| `Serialization` | Encoding/decoding errors |
| `Timeout` | Operation timeout errors |
| `Repository` | Wraps `RepositoryError` via `#[from]` |

### ApplicationError (enhanced)
| Variant | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `Domain(DomainError)` | Business rule violations via `#[from]` |
| `Infrastructure(InfrastructureError)` | External system failures via `#[from]` |
| `Venue(VenueError)` | Venue-specific errors via `#[from]` |
| `Validation(String)` | Input validation failures |
| `NotFound { resource_type, id }` | Resource not found |
| `Unauthorized` | Authentication/authorization failures |

### Helper Methods
- `InfrastructureError::is_retryable()` - Network, Timeout, MessageQueue are retryable
- `ApplicationError::is_retryable()` - Delegates to wrapped Infrastructure/Venue errors
- `ApplicationError::is_not_found()` - Checks NotFound and specific variants
- `ApplicationError::is_validation()` - Checks Validation variant
- `ApplicationError::is_unauthorized()` - Checks Unauthorized variant

## Technical Decisions

- Used thiserror `#[from]` attribute for automatic error conversion
- `InfrastructureError` wraps `RepositoryError` to unify persistence errors
- `ApplicationError` wraps all lower-layer errors (Domain, Infrastructure, Venue)
- Retryability is determined by delegating to wrapped error types
- Renamed `ValidationError` to `Validation` for consistency with new `NotFound` struct variant

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests added (17 new tests, 809 total)
- [x] InfrastructureError: database, network, message_queue, cache, external_service, configuration, serialization, timeout, from_repository_error
- [x] ApplicationError: from_domain_error, from_infrastructure_error, from_venue_error, not_found, unauthorized, is_retryable, is_not_found

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows `.internalDoc/09-rust-guidelines.md`
- [x] Documentation updated (doc comments on all public items)
- [x] No warnings from `cargo clippy`

Closes #43

#### Problem

Dependabot currently doesn't work correctly for docs because `docs` is correctly ignored by the `/` pnpm workspace. This means that dependabot PRs that update docs dependencies fail as they don't update the appropriate lockfile.

#### Summary of Changes

Add a dependabot config for the `/docs` directory

- same schedule as /
- eslint group is different, as we use `eslint` and `eslint-next-config` rather than `@eslint/` and `@typescript-eslint/`
- added `solana` as a group with `@solana/*`. This will capture updates to Kit and web3js. I think this will make dependabot automatically update the kit dependencies which it currently doesn't, probably because they're in the root workspace
- keep the solana-program-client and react groups from root

This might take a little iteration but it's low risk and I think worth it to get one more thing automated properly 

Fixes: broken dependabot PRs hopefully

### Motivation

body:
### Motivation
- Surface pending memory proposals in the web console and allow end-to-end accept/reject actions so proposals created by agents become visible and actionable.
- Replace hardcoded core API origin with a single env var to avoid mixed-hostname issues on WSL/Windows and make fetch errors more actionable.
- Expose and wire proposal endpoints in the Core API and enable CORS for the console origin so the UI can call the API from the browser.

### Description
- Frontend: introduce `VITE_API_BASE_URL` (default `http://localhost:8000`), replace prior hardcoded URL usage, and enrich fetch error messages with HTTP status and body snippets in `apps/web-console/src/api/memory.ts`.
- Frontend: add a Proposals section (table with proposal_id, subject, predicate, object, confidence, source_note, status, created_at) above Facts on the Memory page with `[Accept]` and `[Reject]` actions wired to `acceptProposal`/`rejectProposal`, and refresh facts/proposals after actions in `apps/web-console/src/pages/MemoryPage.tsx`.
- Backend: add `GET /memory/proposals/{proposal_id}` and wire existing proposal list/accept/reject endpoints to the `FactsStore` with consistent serialization in `apps/core-api/app/api/memory.py`.
- Backend: enable CORS for the web console origin (`http://localhost:5173`) in `apps/core-api/app/main.py` and update `docker-compose.yml` to set `VITE_API_BASE_URL` for the web-console service.
- Docs: add a 30s demo script and usage note for `VITE_API_BASE_URL` to `README.md`.
- Tests: add small core-api tests for `get_proposal` and missing-proposal behavior in `apps/core-api/tests/test_memory.py`.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m pytest apps/core-api/tests/test_memory.py`; collection/execute failed with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'app'` (test environment import path issue), so core-api unit tests did not complete successfully.
- Started the web console dev server (`pnpm --filter @lonelycat/web-console dev`) and confirmed the Memory page loads; captured a screenshot of the Memory page via an automated Playwright script which completed successfully.
- Attempted to start the core API with `uvicorn app.main:app` which failed in the current environment due to Python import path (`No module named 'memory'`), so API runtime was not fully validated here.

## Summary

- `npx github:windschord/claude-work` 実行時に、グローバルの Prisma 7.x が使用される問題を修正
- `npx prisma` / `npx pm2` を `node_modules/.bin/` への直接参照に置換
- Windows 対応（`.cmd` 拡張子）も考慮

## Background

`npx prisma` コマンドはグローバルにインストールされた Prisma を使用する可能性があり、Prisma 7.x が利用可能な環境では破壊的変更により以下のエラーが発生していました：

```
The datasource property 'url' is no longer supported in schema files.
```

## Changes

| ファイル | 変更内容 |
|----------|----------|
| `package.json` | `npx prisma generate` → `prisma generate` |
| `src/bin/cli.ts` | `npxCmd` を `prismaCmd` / `pm2Cmd` に置換 |

## Test plan

- [x] CLI ユニットテスト通過
- [x] E2E テストで Prisma 5.22.0 が正しく使用されることを確認
- [x] `node dist/src/bin/cli.js help` 動作確認

body:
## Details
$ #72507

**Problem:** On Android, when pressing the save button, the button floats to the center of the screen during the keyboard dismiss animation. This creates a jarring visual experience.

**Root Cause:** In \FormProvider.tsx\, \KeyboardUtils.dismiss().then(() => onSubmit(...))\ waits for the keyboard to fully hide before executing navigation. On Android, this creates a delay where the UI re-layouts while the button is still visible, causing the floating effect.

**Solution:** Execute navigation immediately on Android before keyboard dismiss, matching iOS behavior where the callback executes at the start of keyboard dismissal.

## Changes
- Added \Platform\ to react-native imports
- Added platform-specific handling in the submit function:
  - On Android: Execute \onSubmit\ first, then dismiss keyboard in background
  - On iOS/other platforms: Keep existing behavior (dismiss then submit)

## Fixed Issues
- $ #72507

## Tests
- [x] Verified code change is minimal and targeted
- [ ] Tested on Android device - save button no longer floats
- [ ] Tested on iOS device - existing behavior preserved

### Motivation
- Prevent spurious zero-priced catalog matches by rejecting candidate meters with non-positive unit prices unless explicitly declared free or allowed by structured hints.

body:
## Summary
This PR addresses volume permission issues in the Docker Compose setup by ensuring the openclaw volume has correct ownership before the main service starts.

## Key Changes
- Added `user` directive to the openclaw-gateway service to run the container with the host user's UID/GID
- Introduced a new `fix-permissions` service that runs before openclaw-gateway to set correct ownership on the shared volume
- Added a `depends_on` constraint to ensure the permission fix completes successfully before the main service starts

## Implementation Details
- The `fix-permissions` service uses a lightweight Alpine image to minimize overhead
- It runs a single `chown` command to set the openclaw volume ownership to `1000:1000` (standard node user)
- The `service_completed_successfully` condition ensures the main service only starts after permissions are properly configured
- The openclaw-gateway service now respects the host user's UID/GID, preventing permission conflicts between the container and host filesystem

body:
Implements validation infrastructure for `data/menu.json` to prevent schema violations and duplicate IDs/SKUs. Adds CI enforcement and normalization tooling.

## Changes

**Validation System**
- `data/menu.schema.json` - JSON Schema draft-07 with required fields, type constraints, and format validation
- `scripts/check_menu.js` - Validates schema compliance and ID/SKU uniqueness using Ajv
- `scripts/normalize_menu.js` - Adds missing required fields (variantes, modificadores, tags, imagenes, calorias_kcal)
- `scripts/list_duplicates.js` - Reports duplicate IDs/SKUs with locations

**Menu Normalization**
- Added missing fields to ~60 products: `variantes: null`, `modificadores: []`, `calorias_kcal: 0`
- Standardized null modificadores to empty arrays
- No duplicates found (141 unique IDs, 141 unique SKUs across 11 categories)

**Linting & CI**
- `.eslintrc.json` - eslint:recommended config for Node.js/ES2021
- Fixed 7 unnecessary regex escape characters in `lib/detect-address.js` and `lib/parse-order.js`
- `.github/workflows/validate-menu.yml` - Runs validation and linting on push/PR
- `docs/VALIDATION.md` - Usage guide and schema requirements

**Package Changes**
- Added devDependencies: `ajv@^8.12.0`, `ajv-formats@^2.1.1`, `eslint@^8.56.0`
- Added scripts: `validate-menu`, `lint`, `lint:fix`

## Schema Design

Products support flexible pricing models:

```json
{
  "precio": 10.00,           // Single price (variantes: null)
  "variantes": null,
  "calorias_kcal": 500
}
```

```json
{
  "precio": null,            // No base price (variants only)
  "variantes": {
    "pequena": 9.00,
    "mediana": 20.90,
    "familiar": 27.90
  },
  "calorias_kcal": {
    "pequena": 650,
    "mediana": 1200,
    "familiar": 1800
  }
}
```

Schema enforces `precio` and `variantes` as oneOf [null, number/object], preventing invalid states.

## Usage

```bash
npm run validate-menu  # Schema + uniqueness checks
npm run lint           # Code style validation
node scripts/normalize_menu.js  # Fix missing fields
```

**Portability fix for docker-diagnostics.sh**

**Consistent credential validation logic**

- Both now enforce hub keys (public + private) are required for Vault authentication

- Previous logic incorrectly allowed operation if *either* hub keys *or* storage keys were present

```cpp
// Before: Allowed operation with partial credentials
if (!has_hub_keys && !has_storage_keys) { /* fail */ }

// After: Strictly requires hub keys for authentication
if (hub_credentials_missing) { /* fail */ }

# What’s new in this PR?
Tightened the shake detection logic to prevent accidental navigation to the logs screen after unlocking.

### Issues
App sometimes opens the log management screen after the device is unlocked while Wire stays in foreground.

### Causes (Optional)
Shake detection was too sensitive to brief accelerometer spikes during unlock/resume, and triggered on a single spike.

### Solutions
- Added a short post‑resume ignore window.

body:
## Summary
This PR improves error handling and resource management across three crates by adding panic safety to the HTTP tracker callback, converting thread-local storage to thread-safe synchronization primitives, and optimizing cache flushing logic.

## Key Changes

### nimble-net/tracker_http.rs
- Wrapped the entire `status_callback` function body in `std::panic::catch_unwind()` to prevent panics from propagating across the FFI boundary into WinHTTP
- Added panic recovery logic that completes the request with an error message if a panic occurs during callback processing
- Ensures proper cleanup of context even when panics occur, preventing resource leaks

### nimble-net/utp.rs
- Converted `PacketPool` from `Rc<RefCell<>>` (single-threaded) to `Arc<Mutex<>>` (thread-safe)
- Updated `UtpSocket::new_outgoing()` and `UtpSocket::new_incoming()` to accept a `PacketPool` parameter instead of creating new pools
- Added `packet_pool` field to `UtpMultiplexer` to manage a shared pool across all sockets
- Updated all test cases to create and pass `PacketPool` instances
- Enables safe sharing of packet buffers across multiple threads and sockets

### nimble-storage/cache.rs
- Optimized `flush_oldest()` to write directly to disk while iterating, rather than collecting writes first
- Changed from `pop_front()` to `front().cloned()` followed by explicit `pop_front()` to avoid unnecessary moves
- Simplified `flush_all()` with the same pattern for consistency
- Reduces memory allocations and improves cache flushing efficiency

## Implementation Details
- The panic handling in `status_callback` preserves the original behavior for non-panic cases while safely handling unexpected panics
- The `PacketPool` changes maintain backward compatibility at the API level while enabling better resource sharing
- Cache flushing changes maintain the same semantics while reducing intermediate allocations

author: sasswart
body:
When the `WithRequestBody` option is passed to `NewRequestConfig`, the `body` parameter is usually not used. It is however still serialized, regardless of whether it is used or overwritten by the option. This is a redundant use of CPU and memory.

For larger requests (ie. fuller contexts), the cost of redundant serialization adds up and eventually dominates the cost of requests sent.

In this PR, we skip serialization if a request body reader has already been specified using the `WithRequestBody` option.

Attached benchmarks show, somewhat dramatically, a 99% reduction in allocations and allocated bytes. Real world results show a more moderate 30-50% reduction, which is still noteworthy.

Benchmarks were generated as follows:

git checkout main -- internal/requestconfig/requestconfig.go

benchstat before.txt after.txt

author: csansoon
body:
## Summary
PromptL now intelligently treats `---` as regular text when it cannot be a valid config section delimiter, eliminating unnecessary errors.

Previously, any occurrence of `---` in a document would be parsed as a config delimiter, forcing users to escape it as `\---` even in cases where it clearly couldn't be config (e.g., after the config section was already closed, or when there was content before it).

With this change:
- `---` appearing after a config section has been closed is treated as text
- `---` appearing after any substantive content (text, tags, mustache expressions) is treated as text
- Comments and whitespace before `---` still allow it to be parsed as config

This aligns parsing behavior with the specification that config must be at the top of the file, making prompt authoring more intuitive.

author: girinath01
body:
### Motivation
- Provide automated scenario validation by scanning Loki logs so the lab can detect expected signals for each scenario. 
- Expose a downloadable report and a one-click lab reset to streamline training/assessment workflows. 
- Surface validation status in the UI so users can see progress and download evidence without inspecting telemetry manually.

### Description
- Added a Loki helper `loki_recent` and three new Portal API endpoints in `apps/portal-api/app/main.py`: `GET /api/validate`, `GET /api/report`, and `POST /api/lab/reset`, and updated `/api/activity` to use the helper. 
- The validation logic inspects recent `ot-sim` logs for simple signal patterns and returns per-scenario detection state and a completion summary. 
- Added UI changes in `apps/portal-ui/src/main.jsx` to register a new `Validation` sidebar tab, fetch validation data on refresh, and provide `Download Report` and `Reset Lab` actions. 
- Added documentation and assets: `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and placeholder screenshots under `docs/screenshots/`.

### Testing
- No automated test suite was executed as part of this change. 
- An end-to-end screenshot attempt using Playwright to capture the Validation tab was run and failed due to a Chromium crash in the environment (browser process SIGSEGV). 
- Manual verification steps are documented in the README (start with `docker compose --profile full up -d` and exercise `GET /api/validate`, `GET /api/report`, and `POST /api/lab/reset`).

### Motivation
- Make the calculation behind Table 4 (Team Proficiency Over Time) explicit so readers can trace how monthly proficiency percentages are derived from the inputs in Sections 1–3.

### Description
- Add a new Section 5 (`#step-5`) titled "How Table 4 Is Calculated (Deep Dive)" that documents the full calculation flow from quarterly product rates to monthly proficiency percentages. 
- Document the steps: expand quarterly rates to months, estimate required headcount via linear interpolation between product-level staffing rows, compute monthly hires as `max(required - prior total headcount, 0)`, split hires into high-fit/low-fit using the `Internal hiring (%)` share, apply the training curves from Section 3 to each hire cohort, and compute `Proficiency % = effective capacity ÷ total headcount` for each month. 
- This change is purely documentation in `index.html` and does not modify the model logic or scripts.

### Testing
- Launched a local server with `python -m http.server 8000` and confirmed the site served successfully. 
- Captured a visual verification screenshot using a Playwright script (`from playwright.sync_api import sync_playwright`) which produced `artifacts/table-4-explanation.png` successfully.

Enhances LFO modulator usability by increasing slider precision, adding visual feedback, and providing fine-grained loop start control. Addresses 4:3 aspect ratio layout issues.

## Changes

- **Offset calculation**: `int((fine_tune / 100.0) * 0.01 * frame_count)` provides 0-1% frame offset

target_idx = (base_start + mod_offset + fine_tune_offset + int(prog * loop_frames)) % self.frame_count

body:
### Motivation
- Railway builds were failing due to the environment not being detected as a normal Node project and the repo containing no explicit Node engine/start metadata, so the build needed Node metadata and a simple start command.
- The Telegram bot was sending fixed/old messages and had duplicated/unclear scheduling, so the project needed a single daily scheduler that delegates message content to the bot route and sending to the Telegram helper.
- The goal was to make the automatic daily summary reliable (22:00 America/Argentina/Tucuman), avoid sending when configuration is missing, and expose scheduler health information.

### Description
- Add Node version metadata and start command by creating `.nvmrc` with `18` and adding `engines.node: 18.x` plus a root `start` script, and add the same `engines` entry in `backend/package.json` to ensure Railway uses Node instead of mise.
- Replace the old inline scheduler behavior with a single daily scheduler in `backend/server.js` that logs status, exposes `version` and scheduler state on `/api/health`, and calls the exported `sendDailySummaryInternal` from `backend/routes/bot.js` once per day at 22:00 Tucumán time.
- Refactor `backend/routes/bot.js` so `sendDailySummaryInternal()` builds the real summary from `transactions type='LOAD'` (today in TZ America/Argentina/Tucuman), formats the message as the specified summary, returns a `{ skipped: true, reason }` object when `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` or chat id is missing, and makes the `/api/bot/daily-summary?secret=...` endpoint return `400` when skipped or `200` with the summary when delivered.
- No changes were made to `backend/bot/telegram.js` besides using it unchanged for sending; no database schema changes were performed.

### Testing
- No automated tests were added or executed as part of this change.
- Basic CI/build-focused adjustments are limited to engine/start metadata to allow Railway to build with standard Node detection (manual deployment verification recommended).

author: copilot
body:
The `getPointsVia()` query scans large tables inefficiently when searching for packets transmitted via a specific digipeater. Query plan starts with AprsPacket INNER JOIN on unindexed LIKE conditions.

## Changes

**Query restructuring:**
- Changed INNER JOIN to EXISTS subquery to filter PosReport first by indexed columns (rtime, position)
- Added DISTINCT to handle multiple AprsPacket matches per position
- Removed redundant time predicates in subquery

**Before:**
```sql
SELECT r.position 
FROM "AprsPacket" p 
INNER JOIN "PosReport" r ON p.src=r.src AND p.time=r.rtime 
WHERE p.time > ? AND p.time < ? 
AND (p.path LIKE ? || '*%' OR ...)
```

**After:**
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT r.position 
FROM "PosReport" r 
WHERE r.rtime > ? AND r.rtime < ? 
AND EXISTS (
  SELECT 1 FROM "AprsPacket" p 
  WHERE p.src = r.src AND p.time = r.rtime 
  AND (p.path LIKE ? || '*%' OR ...)
)
```

**Indexes added:**
- `posreport_src_rtime_idx` on (src, rtime) - composite for join
- `aprspacket_path_idx` on (path text_pattern_ops) - prefix LIKE support
- `aprspacket_ipath_idx` on (ipath text_pattern_ops) - prefix LIKE support

**Schema:**
- Version 13 → 14
- Upgrade script handles existing databases

Potential fix for [https://github.com/cyr-ius/heatzypy/security/code-scanning/5](https://github.com/cyr-ius/heatzypy/security/code-scanning/5)

In general, to fix clear-text logging of sensitive information, you should avoid logging data structures that might contain secrets (passwords, tokens, API keys), or you should sanitize/redact those fields before logging. For HTTP clients, this usually means not logging full request bodies for authentication endpoints, or logging only non-sensitive metadata like path and method.

For this code, the safest, least invasive change is to adjust the debug log in `async_request` so that it does not include `kwargs.get("json")` for requests that may contain sensitive data. Since `async_get_token` always uses `path="login"` and that is where the password is present, we can special-case the `login` path to avoid logging the JSON body at all, or log only redacted information. To preserve functionality while eliminating sensitive-data logging, we can log the payload only when the path is not `login`. This can be done by computing a `log_body` variable that is `None` (or a redaction string) when `path == "login"`, and otherwise equal to `kwargs.get("json")`, and then using that in the debug statement. No new imports are needed, and the change is limited to the `logger.debug` call around line 65 in `heatzypy/auth.py`.

Concretely:
- In `heatzypy/auth.py`, in `async_request`, replace the single `logger.debug("Request: %s (%s) - %s", path, method, kwargs.get("json"))` line with two lines:
  - One to derive a safe representation: e.g., `log_body = None if path == "login" else kwargs.get("json")`.
  - One to log using `log_body`.
This keeps all behavior the same except that the login request body is not logged.

author: maxkless
body:
Nx Console surfaced some issues with the current Nx daemon and was creating them.
- The startup sequence in intellij is starting two new daemons which surfaced this bug: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/pull/34284 - we have to wait for it to be available in nx in order to use the new watcher flow effectively
- In IntelliJ, we weren't waiting for the workspace to actually refresh before giving a success notification - this is fixed
- there were possible race conditions which would start 2 daemon instances - this is fixed with more defensive programming in `ensureDaemonIsStarted`. We still make sure to spawn the daemon process NOT in a subprocess of the nxls - this can cause editor hanging issues otherwise because the daemon process is supposed to be long-lived
- watcher events triggering could cause simultaneous project graph recomputations. This is fixed by deferring to the in-progress computation if a new one comes in.

author: charles-typ
body:
Summary: The benchmark server was not scaling with multiple clients (2 clients at 388K QPS each vs 1 client at 686K QPS) due to CacheLib lock contention. The lock_power was hardcoded to 16 (65K locks) while hash_power defaults to 20 (1M buckets), causing ~16 hash buckets to share each lock. This change makes lock_power match hash_power to achieve a 1:1 ratio, matching production ucache configuration and eliminating the contention bottleneck.

body:
This PR implements Phase A of the "Absolute Final Master Prompt" to repair trust in the platform's verdicts.

Key Changes:
1.  **World Model (Engine 41 & 65):** Introduced a "Ground Truth" module (`world_model.ts`) that defines `REALITY_ANCHORS` (e.g., Google, Amazon) as immune to casual suspicion.
2.  **Trusted Brand Immunity (Engine 45):** The system now strictly prevents trusted domains from being flagged as "Suspicious" or "Malicious" unless specific abuse patterns (like phishing on Google Docs) are detected.
3.  **Confidence Governor (Engine 50 & 60):** Implemented strict confidence ranges (e.g., Legitimate 85-98%, Suspicious 40-70%) and prohibited 100% confidence to maintain epistemic honesty.
4.  **Verdict Consistency Guard (Engine 63):** The Orchestrator now downgrades verdicts if the confidence score does not support the severity, preventing logical contradictions.
5.  **Human-Centric Explanations (Engine 36 & 44):** Explanations now include specific `UserImpact` (Worst Case, Likelihood) and `UserGuidance` (Immediate Action), ensuring the output is actionable and calm.

These changes ensure that `google.com` is consistently rated as `SAFE` (Legitimate) and that the system behaves as a "decision support system" rather than just a scanner.

### Motivation
- Rain totals on the Extremes page were being computed incorrectly (was using `max(rain)-min(rain)`), so reported totals could be zero or wrong for intervals. 
- MIN/MAX graphing did not consistently apply the SUM-based aggregation and unit scaling for rainfall, leading to incorrect min/max/avg values shown for rain series.

### Description
- In `frontend/extremes.php` replaced `round(max(archive.rain)-min(archive.rain),1)` with `round(sum(archive.rain) * 10, 1)` so rain totals are summed over the interval and converted to the same display units. 
- In `frontend/dynamic-graph.php` updated the `MINMAX` and `AVG` query paths to choose the appropriate aggregation (`SUM` when `$calc === 'SUM'`, otherwise `AVG`) and apply the `units` scaling to the average, min and max columns so all three series are consistently scaled. 
- Updated prepared statement parameter binding to pass the scaling factor for all three returned columns (`mysqli_stmt_bind_param(..., 'ddd', $units, $units, $units)`).

author: nminhnguyen
body:
Supports #177.

MUI's `Container` component renders a `<div>` with:
- `width: 100%` + `margin: 0 auto` (centering)
- Horizontal gutters: `16px`, bumped to `24px` at `≥600px`
- `maxWidth="lg"` caps width at `1200px` (at `≥1200px` viewports)
- `sx={{ py: 3 }}` adds `24px` vertical padding (MUI spacing: `3 × 8px`)

The Tailwind replacement:

```
<div className="mx-auto max-w-300 px-4 py-6 sm:px-6">
```

| MUI style | Tailwind class | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `margin: 0 auto` | `mx-auto` | centers the container |
| `padding-left/right: 16px` | `px-4` | `16px` |
| `@media (≥600px) { px: 24px }` | `sm:px-6` | `24px` at `≥640px` |
| `@media (≥1200px) { max-width: 1200px }` | `max-w-300` | `1200px` (exact match) |
| `sx={{ py: 3 }}` → `padding-top/bottom: 24px` | `py-6` | `24px` |

Omitted from MUI:
- `width: 100%` — redundant on a block-level `div`
- `@media (≥1200px)` wrapper for `max-width` — redundant since `max-w-300` has no effect when the viewport is already narrower than 1200px

Minor difference: gutter breakpoint shifts from 600px to 640px (Tailwind `sm`), which has no impact on any real device.

author: aleksa2105
body:
This pull request introduces a comprehensive driver activity logging system, enabling drivers to toggle their activity status and track their daily active time. The backend now manages daily driver logs, enforces business rules (such as preventing status changes during ongoing rides), and exposes new API endpoints. The frontend integrates with these APIs, allowing drivers to change their status and ensuring correct logout behavior. Additionally, several supporting DTOs, mappers, and exception classes are added.

**Backend: Driver Daily Log Feature**

* Added `DriverDailyLogController` with endpoints for drivers to change their status and retrieve today's log.
* Implemented `DriverDailyLogService` to manage daily logs, handle status changes, and enforce business logic (e.g., cannot go inactive during an ongoing ride).
* Created `DriverDailyLogRepository`, DTO (`DriverDailyLogResponse`), mapper (`DriverDailyLogMapper`), and exception (`DriverDailyLogNotFoundException`) to support the new feature.
* Enhanced `DriverDailyLog` entity with methods to manage activation state and active time calculation.
* Updated CORS configuration to allow PATCH requests.

**Backend: Integration and Auth Changes**

* On driver login, the system now automatically sets the driver's status to active by updating the daily log.
* Added repository method to check for ongoing rides before allowing status changes.

**Frontend: Driver Status Management**

* Introduced `DriverDailyLogService` in Angular to interact with backend status endpoints.
* Refactored driver actions component to use a reactive signal for status, call the backend for status changes, and enforce business rules during logout (e.g., cannot logout while active).
* Updated the driver actions UI to reflect the new reactive status and error handling.

**Other Changes**

* Renamed `isActive` to `active` in `ChangeDriverStatusRequest` for consistency.
* Removed unused status change endpoint from `DriverController` (now handled by the new controller).

author: anthony-spruyt
body:
## Summary

- Adds `persist-credentials: false` to all `actions/checkout` steps in CI workflow

## Problem

The per-command `-c url.insteadOf` auth approach fails in CI because `actions/checkout` with `persist-credentials: true` (default) bakes the `GITHUB_TOKEN` into a global git config:

```
url."https://x-access-token:TOKEN@github.com/".insteadOf = "https://github.com/"
```

This causes the remote URL to contain embedded credentials that don't match our `insteadOf` patterns, resulting in:

```
fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': No such device or address
```

## Solution

Setting `persist-credentials: false` prevents `actions/checkout` from configuring global git credentials, allowing our per-command auth to work as designed.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (lint, build, unit tests)
- [ ] Integration tests pass on main after merge (GitHub PAT flow)
- [ ] GitHub App integration tests pass

Fixes #323

body:
This PR introduces a Visual Editor for the Admin Dashboard's JSON file browser. It allows non-technical users to easily edit simple configuration files (like `manias.json` or `music_blacklist.json`) using a table-based interface instead of raw JSON.

**Features:**
- **Mode Toggle:** Users can switch between "Raw Editor" (textarea) and "Visual Editor" (table).
- **Structure Detection:** Automatically detects if the JSON is a flat List or a flat Dictionary. If the structure is too complex (nested objects, mixed types), the Visual Editor is disabled to ensure safety.
- **CRUD:** Users can Add new rows, Delete existing rows, and Edit keys/values directly in the table.
- **Safety:** Changes are synced back to the raw editor before saving. Invalid inputs are handled gracefully.
- **Theme:** Integrated with the existing dark mode/Cthulhu theme.

**Verified:**
- Verified via Playwright script that the editor correctly loads, toggles, adds rows, and saves changes for both Lists and Dictionaries.
- Verified backend API remains compatible.

The new building CI system will compile all filters list definition files [^1] and publish the output to npmjs.com.

[^1]: During compilation, `!#include` directives are merged and `!#if` directives are processed, resulting in a merged-only version and a fully processed version.

This change ensures filters list integrity by preventing clients from loading mismatched file versions caused by a CDN purge issue.

author: kenzonyeoh
body:
- Switched to using [CodeMirror 6](https://codemirror.net/) due to its better accessibility and less buggy implementation of features like word wrap. Monaco seems overkill for what we need, as many of its features are unnecessary, whereas codemirror's modularity means we can pick and choose.
- Tried to fix the directory listing bug that sometimes occurs when browsing, by changing loadDirect to run in $effect instead of onMount. The former runs whenever $props and $state changes, while the latter only runs once. I am unsure if that's what's contributing to the bug as it only intermittently happens, but this seems like a very plausible cause.

author: sirtenzin
body:
--- ## Summary by cubic Adds Tinybird-backed pagination to the external Events API and switches aggregation/listing to Tinybird for faster, consistent analytics. Also fixes command bar impersonation and streamlines event selection in the UI. - **New Features** - Added Tinybird pipe list_events_paginated and server bindings; new POST /events/list supports offset/limit, filters (customer_id, feature_ids, date range), and returns has_more. - External aggregation now uses Tinybird (enforceGroupLimit for API); added validation for group_by property paths and kept internal truncation behavior. - Unified/renamed internal handlers and routed legacy analytics to the new external aggregate handler; added enforceGroupLimit to TimeseriesEventsParams. - UI updates: event dropdown now selects by event_names with linked feature labels; customer analytics and timeseries hooks default to cached event names when none provided. - **Bug Fixes** - Command bar impersonation: run org/user searches concurrently, prioritize organizations in results, and impersonate the first org user reliably. - Analytics view: removed topEvents dependency to prevent empty-state/loader glitches and reduce flicker. Written for commit d90fd59b9905f2fab861258e2bed5c8dcb61e738. Summary will update on new commits.

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

 This PR migrates event querying from direct ClickHouse queries to Tinybird pipes, introducing a new paginated event listing endpoint for the external API. ## Key Changes **Improvements:** - Implemented new `list_events_paginated` Tinybird pipe with offset-based pagination for external API - Added `listEventsForApi` action to serve paginated raw events through the external API - Migrated `aggregate` action to use Tinybird pipes (`aggregateSimple` and `aggregateGroupable`) instead of direct ClickHouse queries - Refactored frontend `CommandBar.tsx` to use `useQueries` for parallel org/user search requests, improving performance - Simplified `SelectFeatureDropdown` to use `useEventNames` hook instead of deprecated `getTopEventNames` function **API changes:** - Added new POST `/events/list` endpoint for paginated event listing - Added `enforceGroupLimit` parameter to `TimeseriesEventsParams` type - Removed `topEvents` from analytics responses across frontend and backend **Improvements:** - Renamed handler files to distinguish internal vs external API handlers (`handleInternalAggregateEvents`, `handleExternalAggregateEvents`, etc.) - Renamed `server/src/internal/analytics/actions/index.ts` to `eventActions.ts` for better clarity - Updated test imports to reflect renamed modules - Cleaned up unused `useTopEventNames` hook and related state management The migration maintains backward compatibility while improving query performance through Tinybird's optimized pipes.

Confidence Score: 5/5

- This PR is safe to merge with minimal risk - Score reflects well-structured migration from ClickHouse to Tinybird pipes with clear separation of concerns, proper error handling, consistent naming conventions, comprehensive test coverage, and frontend optimizations that improve performance without breaking existing functionality - No files require special attention

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | server/src/external/tinybird/pipes/listEventsPaginatedPipe.ts | New pipe for paginated event listing with offset/limit support | | server/tinybird/pipes/list_events_paginated.pipe | New Tinybird SQL pipe for paginated event queries | | server/src/internal/analytics/actions/listEventsForApi.ts | New action implementing paginated event listing for external API | | server/src/internal/analytics/actions/aggregate.ts | Updated to use Tinybird pipes instead of direct ClickHouse queries | | server/src/internal/events/handlers/handleExternalAggregateEvents.ts | Renamed from `handleAggregateEvents.ts` and updated to use Tinybird-based aggregate | | server/src/internal/events/handlers/handleExternalListEvents.ts | New handler for external API event listing using `listEventsForApi` | | vite/src/views/command-bar/CommandBar.tsx | Refactored to use `useQueries` for parallel org and user search requests | | vite/src/views/customers/customer/analytics/components/SelectFeatureDropdown.tsx | Refactored to use `useEventNames` instead of `getTopEventNames`, simplified to only use event names |

Based on #44.

With https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh-proxy-utils/pull/8, `iroh-proxy-utils` has full `HTTP/2` support on the downstream, support for removing hop-by-hop headers, and improved request handling. Request handling is now a single trait, no fixed separation between forward and reverse modes anymore. Hop-by-hop headers are removed automatically. While migrating, I removed the the old n0des based interface for the gateway. I can add it back also, but I think it's being phased out anyway, right?

author: zhongzhijie1
body:
Bug: v/83024

This PR fixes several GATT client issues when working with Zephyr / zblue stack.

Some stacks do not support parallel GATT discovery.
Some apps also call discover_service_by_uuid many times.
And Zephyr needs CCC handle for CCCD, not value handle.

These problems make service DB broken and CCCD fail.

This PR includes three related changes.

--------------------------------
1. Serialize GATT discovery

Some stacks (for example zblue) do not support parallel discovery.
We now make if_gattc_discover_service transactional and per-connection serialized.

When a discovery is running:
- new discover requests are queued
- they will start one by one after DISCOVER_CMPL
- all pending discovers are cleared on disconnect

Each queued request keeps its own filter_uuid,
so it runs with the original parameters.

--------------------------------
2. Use single service DB in gattc_service

sal_gatt_client resets element index on every discover call.
So results from bt_sal_gatt_client_discover_service_by_uuid() cannot be accumulated.
After discovery, the service DB becomes incomplete.
Read / write by handle, especially CCCD, may fail.

Now service data is copied by malloc and passed to gattc_service.c.
gattc_service.c owns and frees this memory.
So the GATT service DB is complete and stable.

Future direction:
Only gattc_service.c will keep the service DB.
sal_gatt_client will only use temporary data during discovery.
This part is still TBD.

--------------------------------
3. Add CCC handle query for Zephyr

Zephyr stack needs CCC handle to do CCCD.
Old stack only needs value handle.

A helper is added in gattc_service.c.
It uses the full service DB to map value_handle to ccc_handle.
sal can use it to find the correct CCC handle.

Together these changes fix:
- lost discover results
- broken service DB
- CCCD failure on Zephyr stack

author: bgrady-tt
body:
Fixed handling of _GenericOp_ outputs that are views/streams requiring virtual grid support. This allows applying arbitrary views to a GenericOp output.

Viewed outputs do not require virtual grid forward and inverse affine maps align with L1 storage (in general reblocked case, this is impossible anyway), so verification is relaxed somewhat.

Refactored how physical grid shapes are queried; it isn't possible to determine if a `MetalLayoutAttr` is a view by itself, so it is necessary to have a free function `d2m::utils::getPhysicalGridShape` that traces memref/tensor _Values_ to disambiguate views from raw memref/tensors.

Cleaned up GenericOp::build logic for determining how to infer inverse virtual grid maps.

author: baogorek
body:
## Summary

- Fixes state/CD calibration using stale 2022-2023 targets instead of correct 2024 values
- Removes hardcoded `CBO_YEAR` and `TREASURY_YEAR` constants from `etl_national_targets.py`
- Adds `--dataset` CLI argument to specify the source dataset
- Derives `time_period` from `sim.default_calculation_period` - the dataset itself is now the single source of truth
- Cherry-picks ACA PTC target ingestion from #508 to keep database and calibration package in sync

## Root Cause

The ETL had hardcoded year constants:
```python
CBO_YEAR = 2023  # was pulling 2023 CBO values
TREASURY_YEAR = 2023  # was pulling 2023 Treasury values
```

But the calibration runs at `time_period=2024`. This caused an 18% gap for income tax alone ($2,051B vs $2,426B).

## The Fix

Instead of hardcoding years, we now derive the time period from the dataset:
```python
sim = Microsimulation(dataset=args.dataset)
time_period = int(sim.default_calculation_period)  # e.g., 2024
```

This ensures CBO/Treasury targets always match the dataset's year, preventing future drift when updating to new base years annually.

## Cherry-picked from #508

This PR includes the ACA PTC database changes from #508 (Add ACA Premium Tax Credit targets from IRS SOI data). This was cherry-picked so that the calibration package could be rebuilt with the updated database and validated end-to-end in Stratified mode (436 CDs).

## Usage

```bash
# Default: uses HuggingFace production dataset
python policyengine_us_data/db/etl_national_targets.py

# Or specify a local dataset
python policyengine_us_data/db/etl_national_targets.py \
  --dataset /path/to/stratified_extended_cps.h5
```

## Test plan

- [x] Run `make database` to regenerate policy_data.db
- [x] Verify CBO/Treasury targets now show 2024 values
- [x] Verify `income_tax` target is ~$2,426B (not $2,051B)
- [x] Rebuild calibration package in Stratified mode (436 CDs) -- verified 18,435 targets, 39 included groups, no errors

Closes #503

author: wolofzhang-hash
body:
### Motivation
- Ensure replay uses all recorded driver angles so animations match saved simulation frames. 
- Prevent modifications or file operations from corrupting an ongoing animation by requiring the animation to stop (with user confirmation) before loading snapshots, opening/creating files, or applying model edits. 

### Description
- Parse serialized lists/dicts in run CSV rows so `driver_deg` entries like "[0.0, 10.0]" are loaded as Python lists using `json.loads`/`ast.literal_eval` (update in `planar_sketch/ui/analysis_tabs.py`).
- Add replay control helpers `is_replay_active()` and `confirm_stop_replay(action)` to the animation tab to prompt the user to stop playback and stop the replay when confirmed (in `analysis_tabs.py`).
- Add `_confirm_stop_replay(action)` to `SketchController` and make `load_dict` return a boolean and accept an `action` description, so callers can be blocked if the user declines to stop playback (in `planar_sketch/core/controller.py`).
- Guard model-editing commands and a number of public model-modification entry points to call `_confirm_stop_replay(...)` and abort if the user does not allow stopping the animation, covering many `cmd_*` methods and drag/move operations (in `controller.py`).
- Call the guarded `load_dict(..., action=...)` from UI file operations and run-snapshot loading so opening/creating files or loading run snapshots asks to stop playback first (in `planar_sketch/ui/main_window.py` and `analysis_tabs.py`).
- Minor ordering/return fixes in `load_dict` to ensure status updates and a boolean success result.

### Testing
- No automated tests were run for this change.

([#​8415](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8415), [@​cert-manager-bot](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager-bot))
-   Fixed an issue where HTTP-01 challenges failed when the Host header containing an IPv6 address. This means that users can now issue IP address certificates for IPv6 address subjects. ([#​8436](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8436), [@​cert-manager-bot](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager-bot))
-   Security (MODERATE): Fix a potential panic in the cert-manager controller whn a DNS response in an unexpected order was cached. If an attacker was able to modify DNS responses (or if they controlled the DNS server) it was possible to cause denial of service for the cert-manager controller. ([#​8468](https://redirect.github.com/cert-manager/cert-manager/issues/8468), [@​SgtCoDFish](https://redirect.github.com/SgtCoDFish))

### What does this PR do?

Fixes the nvkind cluster creation command to delete the cluster if it fails, to ensure that pulumi can re-try the creation correctly.

## Motivation

When developing changes for the nvkind component, if the creation fails the cluster can be left over, and then subsequent creation attempts will fail because the cluster already exists. To fix that, it requires manual intervention. With this fix, we can iterate on fixes in the code without manually intervening if something is wrong.

### Describe how you validated your changes

Manually tested by forcing the command to fail and ensuring that the state is kept clean.

author: severin-richner
body:
# Summary
Adds a small timer TUI utility, which integrates with waybar and has the ability to do pomodoro-style timers.

## Why
I find it useful to have a little timer, which I can directly see in the waybar while working. This addition is meant to do exactly that and nothing more.

## Demo
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32c6ca64-f1b7-4dee-b690-78f9e78d06ba

## Implementation Details and Limitations
The timer functionality essentially consists of 2 scripts. 

The `omarchy-timer` script provides the user interface and the CLI for setting a timer and launches a secondary script, which plays the sound and sends the notification when the timer runs out. It also implements the pomodoro logic, in which the timer simply oscillates between work and break time.

The `timer.sh` script handles the waybar indicator for displaying the active timer.

These two scripts use the `/run/user/$UID/omarchy-active-timer` file to communicate between them. The `omarchy-timer` script writes to this file the current active timers type (`t`:  timer, `w`: work or `b`: break) and the time at which this timer expires in UNIX time. A timer can be canceled by deleting this file, which can be done by right-clicking on the waybar indicator.

### Notifications
- if system is active and timer expires: plays sound and shows notification
- if system is locked and timer expires: plays sound (and triggers notification, however this is not visible on lock screen)
- if system is suspended and timer expires: nothing happens, whenever the system wakes up, the sound and notification are triggered
- if timer is active and user logs out or system shuts down: `/run/user/$UID/` directory gets cleared, thus timer is deleted

[Related Discussion: Incorporate a tui Pomodoro timer #4068](https://github.com/basecamp/omarchy/discussions/4068#discussion-9304565)

author: cesmag
body:
## Summary

Implements **Phase 1: SPILink Foundation** with basic HARQ protocol for SPI transport, addressing the critical architecture gap identified in the QA audit report.

**Architecture Compliance**: 60% → 85% (Phase 1 of 3)

This PR completes the first phase of the 3-phase plan to achieve 100% architecture compliance for dual-transport mode (USB CDC + SPI).

## Changes

### New Files

- **`star-gateway/internal/link/spi.go`** (~700 lines)
  - SPILink implementation with full HARQ protocol
  - ACK/NACK handshake with 10ms timeout
  - Automatic retransmission (max 3 attempts)
  - Shared SessionState with CDCLink (prevents sequence desync during failover)
  - Thread-safe Send() with sendMutex
  - FEC disabled for Phase 1 (will be enabled in Phase 2)

- **`star-gateway/internal/link/spi_test.go`** (~1000 lines)
  - 18 comprehensive unit tests
  - Mock transport for isolated testing
  - Tests for ACK/NACK scenarios, retries, context cancellation, shared state
  - 74.8% code coverage (decodeFEC is Phase 2, excluded)

### Modified Files

- **`star-gateway/internal/app/gateway.go`**
  - Updated `createSPILink()` to use new SPILink implementation
  - Added fallback to legacy ChaseCombining for compatibility
  - Phase 1 configuration: FEC disabled, ACK timeout 10ms, max 3 retries

## Key Features

### HARQ Protocol
- ✅ ACK/NACK handshake for reliable delivery
- ✅ Automatic retransmission on NACK or timeout
- ✅ Smart drain logic via FailureType classification
- ✅ 10ms ACK timeout with exponential backoff

### Shared SessionState
- ✅ Prevents sequence desynchronization during transport switching
- ✅ Shared TX and RX counters between USB CDC and SPI
- ✅ Zero sequence gaps during failover (fixes "Handoff Problem")

### Thread Safety
- ✅ sendMutex ensures atomic sequence assignment + write
- ✅ stateMu protects HARQ state machine
- ✅ Context-aware operations with cancellation support

## Testing

### Unit Tests (18 tests, all passing)
```bash
go test ./internal/link -v -run TestSPILink
```

**Test Coverage**: 74.8%
- NewSPILink: 100.0%
- Send(): 91.4%
- Receive(): 68.2%
- sendAck/sendNack: 80.0%
- HARQ interface: 66.7-80.0%
- decodeFEC: 0.0% (Phase 2, not tested in Phase 1)

### Integration Tests
```bash
go test ./internal/link ./internal/manager ./internal/harq
```
All core transport layer tests pass with no regressions.

## Implementation Details

### Phase 1 Scope (This PR)
- ✅ Basic HARQ with ACK/NACK handshake
- ✅ Retransmission logic (max 3 attempts)
- ✅ Shared SessionState integration
- ✅ HARQ interface implementation
- ✅ Comprehensive unit tests
- ❌ FEC (Forward Error Correction) - Phase 2
- ❌ Chase Combining - Phase 2
- ❌ Frame type API - Phase 3
- ❌ Hot-plug detection - Phase 3

### Design Patterns

**1. Shared SessionState** (Critical Fix #1)
```go
// Both CDCLink and SPILink use the SAME SessionState instance
session := manager.NewSessionState()
cdcLink := link.NewCDCLink(cdcTransport, session)  // Shared
spiLink := link.NewSPILink(spiTransport, session, config)  // Shared
```

**2. Thread-Safe Send** (Critical Fix #5)
```go
s.sendMutex.Lock()  // Lock covers BOTH operations
seq := s.sessionState.NextTxSequence()  // Atomic
err := s.transport.Send(encodedFrame)    // Atomic
s.sendMutex.Unlock()
```

**3. Smart Drain Logic** (Critical Fix #2)
```go
// ACK timeout triggers failover, hard IO errors drain before switching
if err == ErrACKTimeout {
    return FailureTypeRetriable  // Failover immediately
} else {
    return FailureTypeDrain  // Drain queue first
}
```

## Next Steps

### Phase 2: FEC + Chase Combining (Weeks 3-4)
- Viterbi FEC (K=7, Rate 1/2, NASA polynomials)
- Chase Combining for soft-bit accumulation
- ~10x BER improvement in noisy environments

### Phase 3: Frame Types + Hot-Plug (Week 5)
- SendWithType() API for PING/PONG/RESET frames
- inotify-based USB hot-plug detection
- Automatic transport switching on USB events

## References

- QA Audit Report: 60% architecture compliance
- Related PRs: #242 (Phase 7: Documentation)
- Plan: `/home/star/.claude/plans/staged-cuddling-wall.md`

## Checklist

- [x] Implementation complete for Phase 1
- [x] Unit tests written and passing (74.8% coverage)
- [x] Integration tests pass (no regressions)
- [x] Code follows STAR project style guide
- [x] No AI attribution in commit messages
- [x] Separate PR per phase (as requested)
- [ ] Code review
- [ ] Merge to main before Phase 2

author: joemccann
body:
## Summary

- Adds intelligent backup cleanup: backups are now automatically deleted if no files changed during sync
- Adds `--cleanup-backups` command to remove existing redundant backups (one-time cleanup)
- Preserves backup-first safety model - backups are still created before sync, just removed afterward if identical

## Changes

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `claude-sync-setup.sh` | Added `dirs_are_identical()`, `cleanup_backup_if_unchanged()`, `cleanup_backups()`, new `--cleanup-backups` CLI option |
| `zshrc-functions.sh` | Added `_claude_sync_dirs_identical()`, `_claude_sync_cleanup_backup()` |
| `watch/src/sync.rs` | Added `dirs_are_identical()`, `cleanup_backup_if_unchanged()` |

## How It Works

1. Before sync: Create timestamped backup (existing behavior)
2. Perform sync operation
3. After sync: Compare backup with final `~/.claude` state via SHA-256 checksums
4. If identical → delete backup, log "no changes"
5. If different → keep backup (existing behavior)

## Test plan

- [x] All 26 existing tests pass
- [x] Rust daemon compiles successfully  
- [x] Bash scripts pass syntax check
- [ ] Manual test: Run `--cleanup-backups` to verify redundant backup removal
- [ ] Manual test: Run sync when no changes exist, verify backup is removed
- [ ] Manual test: Run sync with actual changes, verify backup is kept

## Summary

Implements BufferedProcessRunner class that ignores stdout completely and buffers stderr, only outputting it on failure.

## Changes

- Add BufferedProcessRunner class in process_runner.py
- Stdout sent to subprocess.DEVNULL (completely ignored)
- Single thread collects stderr from subprocess.PIPE into buffer
- Only outputs buffered stderr if process exit code is non-zero
- Add 12 comprehensive unit tests covering all scenarios and edge cases
- Export BufferedProcessRunner in __all__

## Design

- Uses subprocess.Popen with threading for async stderr collection
- Maintains synchronous interface for compatibility
- Memory efficient: only buffers stderr (typically small)
- Stdout completely discarded (no memory overhead)
- Proper timeout and error handling

## Testing

- Unit tests verify stderr buffering and conditional output
- Edge cases covered: no output, failure without stderr, multiple lines
- Error propagation tested (CalledProcessError, TimeoutExpired)

The agentic maintenance workflow's expired entity detection needs to identify issues created by agentic workflows. Based on code review feedback, this now uses XML comment markers instead of text pattern matching.

### Change

Updated detection logic in `expired_entity_search_helpers.cjs` to use XML comment markers:

```javascript
// Before: text pattern matching
const agenticPattern = /^> AI generated by/m;
const isAgenticWorkflow = entity.body && agenticPattern.test(entity.body);

// After: XML comment marker detection
const hasWorkflowId = entity.body && entity.body.includes("gh-aw-workflow-id:");
const hasAgenticWorkflow = entity.body && entity.body.includes("gh-aw-agentic-workflow:");
const isAgenticWorkflow = hasWorkflowId || hasAgenticWorkflow;
```

This approach is more reliable and consistent with other workflow detection patterns in the codebase (e.g., `close_older_issues.cjs`).

### Why This Matters

XML comment markers (`<!-- gh-aw-workflow-id: ... -->` or `<!-- gh-aw-agentic-workflow: ... -->`) are the authoritative identifiers for agentic workflow-generated content. Issues without these markers are not managed by agentic workflows and should not be auto-closed.

### Tests Updated

- Added XML comment markers to all existing test cases
- Added test confirming issues without XML markers are correctly filtered out
- Added specific tests for both `gh-aw-workflow-id` and `gh-aw-agentic-workflow` marker types

### Issue #12669 Context

Issue #12669 was not detected because it lacks XML comment markers. This is correct behavior - without these markers, the issue is not managed by an agentic workflow and should not be auto-closed.

author: mikep86
body:
Updates all synonyms filters to use a real memory circuit breaker while building the synonyms map. Memory usage is checked every 1024th synonym rule. We use the field data circuit breaker for this, but in practice it doesn't really matter which child circuit breaker we use because real memory usage is checked by the parent circuit breaker.

Behavior in the event of a circuit breaker trip depends on the `lenient` value:

- If `lenient` is true, then an empty synonyms map is used
- If `lenient` is false, the affected index goes red

In either scenario, users can recover by shrinking the synonym set size (or otherwise reducing memory usage) and reloading the analyzers for the affected index.

> ### 5. Tecnologias e Boas Práticas
> - JavaScript puro (ES6+) ou TypeScript
> - Manipulação DOM para interagir com WhatsApp Web
> - Usar MutationObserver para detectar mudanças na interface do WhatsApp

> - Código comentado e bem estruturado

> - Avisar usuário sobre termos de uso do WhatsApp

### Motivation
- Allineare gli input del lancio dadi generico su un'unica riga e rendere possibile precompilare notazione/modificatore dall'esterno dell'overlay.
- Risolvere il problema di stacking che impediva l'apertura visibile dell'accordione dello storico tiri nell'overlay generico.
- Aprire il popup di lancio dadi per i danni al click del pulsante "fuoco" nella sezione Attacchi in Home.

### Description
- Aggiornato il markup dell'overlay (`src/features/dice-roller/overlay/dice.js`) per mettere la notazione e le etichette in una singola riga, aggiungere attributi `aria` e una classe `diceov-generic-notation` per l'input di notazione.
- Aggiunta la funzione `syncGenericInputsFromNotation` e estesi gli argomenti di `openDiceOverlay` con `notation` e `modifier` per preimpostare l'overlay quando viene aperto da codice esterno.

- Tentativi automatizzati con Playwright per aprire l'overlay e catturare screenshot sono stati eseguiti, ma hanno fallito per timeout / mancata inizializzazione dell'app dovuta a variabile mancante (`supabaseUrl is required`), risultato: fallito per ambiente di esecuzione.

author: copilot
body:
PWA shortcuts with hash URLs (e.g., `/#crm`, `/#microsoft-365`) were not navigating to their target sections. The hash fragment was read once on mount but not on subsequent PWA shortcut launches, and relied on Next.js `asPath` which is unreliable in PWA standalone mode.

## Changes

**Hash navigation (`src/pages/index.jsx`)**
- Read hash from `window.location.hash` (reliable in PWA mode) with `asPath` fallback
- Add `hashchange` event listener to handle PWA shortcut launches
- Use functional state updates to prevent dependency cycles
- Fix tabs array access (`tabs[0]` vs `tabs["0"]`)

**External links handler (`src/utils/pwa/external-links.js`)**
- Detect and skip interception for internal hash links (same origin + path, different hash only)
- Prevents interference with hash navigation while maintaining external link handling

## Configuration

```yaml
pwa:
  shortcuts:
    - name: "CRM"
      url: "/#crm"
      description: "Open CRM section"
```

Hash format follows slugification: `"Microsoft 365"` → `#microsoft-365`

body:
https://github.com/tomasklaen/uosc

#### Testing the changes
- I tested the changes in this PR: **YES**
- been using `uosc` for years

#### New package
- This new package conforms to the [package requirements](https://github.com/void-linux/void-packages/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#package-requirements): **YES**

#### Local build testing
- I built this PR locally for my native architecture, **x86_64-glibc**
- I built this PR locally for these architectures:
  - x86_64-musl

Notes:

- <strike>In order to make this package work out-of-the-box (which I presume to be desired, when installing from a package manager), files are going to be installed into `/etc/mpv`, hence globally. Otherwise the user would have to copy everything manually from e.g. `/usr/share`, in which case I'd recommend using the installation script provided by upstream, which will copy everything needed into one's home directory.</strike>
EDIT: I reconsidered this and opted for the non-global installation, which requires additional steps (see `README.voidlinux`), but is more in line w/ Void's packaging guidelines.

- There is a utility binary called "ziggy" that can be built separately (`go` language), which is mainly used for updating `uosc` locally, but it also implements clipboard support, extra subtitle downloads and maybe some other features. I'm not interested in shipping said binary and bloating the package unnecessarily, since `lua`-`uosc` (which advertises itself as being "minimalist") does everything I need from a UI for `mpv`.

## What does this PR do?

This PR fixes that date overrides of fixed hosts are taken into account for round-robin events. This prevents round-robin events being booked where the fixed hosts are unavailable. 

This PR also fixes that date overrides didn't adjust to different timezones. If the organizer has a date override from 10-11 UTC it always showed the slots from 10-11 open no matter what timezone the attendee has.

Fixes #8207
Fixes #8329

Fixes: #8273

**Environment**: Staging(main branch) / Production

## Type of change

- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

**Date overrides for fixed hosts (round-robin):** 
- Create a round-robin event with one fixed host and host round-robin host
- Create a date override for fixed host (round-robin host should also be available at that time)
- Check available slots of event on the day of the date override, it should only show the slots where fixed host is available
- Test that with different time zones on booking page and on the availabilities of fixed and round-robin host

**Date override timezones issue:** 
- Create a date override 
- Go to the booking page of a personal event 
- Change the timezone to a different one that the availability with the date override is 
- See the available slots of the day with the date override change accordingly 
- Also test with different timezones here

This pull request introduces several improvements and fixes to the multiomics pipeline, focusing on better handling of dataset generation modes, resource management, and file naming consistency. The main changes ensure that the pipeline correctly distinguishes between binsize and regions modes for dataset creation, improves resource lookup for different assays, and standardizes output and log file paths, especially for the MCC workflow.

**Multiomics dataset generation improvements:**

* Added a `fasta_index` field to `MultiomicsConfig` and enforced its requirement when using binsize mode for dataset creation, ensuring proper chromosome size handling.
* Updated logic in `build_multiomics_config` to automatically set `fasta_index` from the first assay's genome config for binsize mode. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-3ffb7c7e1a5ec93e7967baebf494ea6789a358e21522d1ee16ee1abe1d2951d3R1115-R1120) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3ffb7c7e1a5ec93e7967baebf494ea6789a358e21522d1ee16ee1abe1d2951d3R1130)
* Modified output handling to dynamically select between `dataset_bins.h5ad` and `dataset_regions.h5ad` based on the presence of `binsize`, and updated test fixtures to explicitly set regions mode for multiomics tests. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-dda6f0b4be0d3dac8cbbefabd02ffd3f3152138ab6a29adc85fae003cc47a662L707-R716) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f7a4e6a90ecaee227ccc189910eedde58a00c09c86ab1d6a16b48a7cc406cc63L87-R89) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-fed93630768aa39d48e16a0d1dd88abec0987c275e25dd8e73a2629f72b864f0R423-R435) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-bf42b25666abc3c1c892ffc1d3ebbc2893654acd189af6832c94d0c73367c9cbL116-R117)

**Assay resource lookup and management:**

* Improved resource lookup logic in `GenomeResources` to prefer exact matches and handle substring matches for assay keys, ensuring the correct resources are used for each assay type. Also added `fasta_index` to resources. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0b8ac6ed7306e60ad94cf107b851ce04f4d460917de9e898999565458e4d6d01R25) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0b8ac6ed7306e60ad94cf107b851ce04f4d460917de9e898999565458e4d6d01L90-R96) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0b8ac6ed7306e60ad94cf107b851ce04f4d460917de9e898999565458e4d6d01L133-R144)
* Refactored resource dictionaries to clarify base and assay-specific resources, and fixed resource assignments for several assays (e.g., `chip-rx`, `crispr`, `meth`, `snp`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-0b8ac6ed7306e60ad94cf107b851ce04f4d460917de9e898999565458e4d6d01R35-R43) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0b8ac6ed7306e60ad94cf107b851ce04f4d460917de9e898999565458e4d6d01R52-R82)

**MCC workflow output and log file standardization:**

* Standardized output, log, and benchmark file paths for MCC alignment rules, improving consistency and clarity in file organization. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-4de3ae51336a15a338160cbcb3f57d764c8c6e47cbb21ccfc57bb297501a0c64L6-R6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-4de3ae51336a15a338160cbcb3f57d764c8c6e47cbb21ccfc57bb297501a0c64L24-R24) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-4de3ae51336a15a338160cbcb3f57d764c8c6e47cbb21ccfc57bb297501a0c64L34-R35) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-4de3ae51336a15a338160cbcb3f57d764c8c6e47cbb21ccfc57bb297501a0c64L51-R63) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-4de3ae51336a15a338160cbcb3f57d764c8c6e47cbb21ccfc57bb297501a0c64L84-R85) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-af35933f9742a796440997b5fc503cefb2cb3f822dd4314a42197ba3e4b765a8L54-R60)

**Multiomics Snakemake rule fixes:**

* Fixed resource lookup in `make_dataset_regions` and `make_dataset_binsize` rules to use cleaned assay names and correct resource keys, improving compatibility with different assay configurations. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c862a9e6222ff093fcc3074c8a36bd9a413687250f47bc2c9539495317aa248eL14-R15) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-c862a9e6222ff093fcc3074c8a36bd9a413687250f47bc2c9539495317aa248eL44-R44)

author: jaisheesh-2006
body:
#### Description
This PR implements strict validation for `metadata.annotations` values during the `live apply` pipeline.

Previously, the Go unmarshaler silently discarded non-string values (e.g., unquoted booleans like `true` or integers like `123`) because they did not match the expected `map[string]string` schema. This resulted in annotations being dropped from the applied resource without warning.

This change adds a validation step that inspects the raw YAML tags of `RNode`s. It now returns a strict error if any annotation value is not a string, while correctly accepting quoted strings (e.g., `"true"`).

#### Motivation
To prevent silent data loss and configuration drift.

Users frequently mistake YAML types (e.g., writing `enabled: true` instead of `enabled: "true"`). Currently, `kpt` ignores these fields silently. This fix ensures the user receives immediate feedback:

**New Error Output:**
`Error: annotation "example.com/enabled" must be a string, got boolean`

#### Which issue does this PR fix?
Fixes #3784

body:
## :wrench: Problem

We need to add authentication to avoid DDOS on the runner

## :cake: Solution

We’ll add the minimal auth. mechanism possible: just a simple secret token, specified in an envvar, and passed to the server in an Authentication header.

## :rotating_light:  Points to watch/comments

There really should be some tests added… but it’s a bit complex to setup with this multiple containers setup.

## :desert_island: How to test

The README  gives httpie and cURL to properly launch an authenticated request. 
So just 
- add the AUTH_KEY variable to your .env file (the .env.sample provides instructions to do so)
- launch `just run` in a terminal window
- run the curl/http command in another one.

Not passing the Authentication header, or passing an empty/incorrect one should result in a 401 error. 

Passing the proper one should launch the runner – no need to wait for the end of the run, which might fail as this is still a WIP, but it’s unrelated.

author: xerial
body:
## Summary

Add CSS Style DSL and Class toggle utilities following React/Vue conventions:

- **`style` object** extends `DomElement` for dual purpose:
  - CSS style builder: `style(style.display := "flex", style.gap := "8px")`
  - `<style>` tag element: `style("body { margin: 0; }")`
- **Raw style strings**: `style := "display: flex;"` (Tailwind-friendly)
- **Class toggle**: `cls.toggle("active") when condition`
- **65+ type-safe CSS properties**

## Usage

```scala
import wvlet.uni.dom.all.*

val isActive = Rx.variable(false)

div(
  // Grouped CSS properties (React/Vue style)
  style(style.display := "flex", style.gap := "8px"),
  
  // Raw style string (Tailwind-friendly)
  style := "margin: 10px;",
  
  // Class toggle with static/reactive conditions
  cls := "base",
  cls.toggle("active") when isActive
)

// <style> tag element
head(style("body { margin: 0; }"))
```

## Design

The `style` object extends `DomElement("style", ...)` to:
1. Override `HtmlTags.style` without type conflicts
2. Serve as both CSS builder and `<style>` tag
3. Allow `style.display := "flex"` syntax for properties

- [x] CSS class toggle tests (8 test cases)

- While in the contract screen, create a new schedule that has 2 weeks calendar and Europe/Paris timezone.
- From Time Off > Management > Allocations, allocate 1+ paid time off days for the newly created employee that's valid from 01/01/2025.
- From the employee's profile > Time Off, try to take a Monday off.

Issue:
- The user gets a Validation error stating that the "start date" is later than the "end date".

Fix:
- In a 2 weeks calendar, there are 2 lines that are there to separate the first week from the second week (for aesthetic purposes). These lines have "hour_from" and "hour_to" = 0, which are taken into account when calulating the minimum hour to start the day off.
- Add a check to remove lines from calendar that are just there for display purposes.

body:
### Motivation
- Replace expensive per-block THREE.Mesh objects with a compact representation to drastically reduce draw calls and improve FPS. 
- Only render blocks that are exposed to air/water so internal blocks do not waste GPU work. 
- Keep game logic (sand settling, water interactions, collisions, chunk load/unload) intact while moving rendering to chunk-level instancing.

### Description
- Replace occupancy entries to store block objects (`{type,bx,by,bz,chunkKey}`) instead of per-block meshes and change `chunks[].blocks` to a `Map` and `chunks[].meshes` to a `Map` for instanced meshes. 
- Add `isBlockExposed`, `buildChunkMeshes`, `clearChunkMeshes`, `rebuildChunksAround` and `rebuildNeighborChunks` to generate per-chunk `THREE.InstancedMesh` per block type containing only exposed blocks and to rebuild neighbors on edits. 
- Update block lifecycle: `addBlockAt` now registers block objects and triggers chunk rebuilds, `removeBlockData` deletes occupancy and chunk entries and triggers rebuilds, and chunk generation/removal integrates with the new maps and mesh rebuild flow. 
- Update physics and interactions to operate on block objects: `settleSand`, `updateSandPhysicsAround`, `isInWater`, raycast picking (`getBlockFromIntersection`), block placement and removal use instance data instead of mesh userData, and collisions query occupancy blocks.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed for this change.

author: tiulpin
body:
## Summary

Fixes #41. Add `tc agent reboot` command and allow all agent commands to accept agent names in addition to numeric IDs.

## Changes

**API (`internal/api/agents.go`, `internal/api/interface.go`)**
- Add `GetAgentByName()` method for looking up agents by name
- Add `RebootAgent()` method using web UI endpoint (no REST API available)
- Extract `agentDetailFields` constant to avoid duplication

**CLI (`internal/cmd/agent.go`, `internal/cmd/agent_terminal.go`)**
- Add `tc agent reboot` command with `--after-build` and `--yes` flags
- Update all agent commands to accept name or ID: `view`, `enable`, `disable`, `authorize`, `deauthorize`, `jobs`, `move`, `term`, `exec`
- Add `resolveAgent()` and `resolveAgentID()` helpers in `helpers.go`
- Success messages now show agent names instead of IDs

**Tests**
- Add unit tests for name-based resolution and reboot command
- Add integration tests for agent operations

## Design Decisions

- **Web UI endpoint for reboot**: TeamCity has no REST API for agent reboot, so we use `/remoteAccess/reboot.html` form endpoint
- **PathEscape for agent names**: TeamCity prohibits colons and commas in agent names (they conflict with locator syntax), so `url.PathEscape` is sufficient
- **Numeric string ambiguity**: If an agent is literally named "123", it will be interpreted as an ID. This is documented in the helper function.

## Example

```bash
# Reboot by name
tc agent reboot Agent-Linux-01

# Reboot after current build finishes
tc agent reboot Agent-Linux-01 --after-build

# Skip confirmation
tc agent reboot Agent-Linux-01 --yes

# Other commands now accept names too
tc agent view Agent-Linux-01
tc agent enable Agent-Linux-01
tc agent term Agent-Linux-01
```

- [x] Linter passes (`golangci-lint run`)
